servinfo.title: Brake Booster Pressure Sensor Inspection (If Equipped)

item.ptxt: If excessive vacuum is applied, the brake booster pressure sensor may be damaged.
Do not exceed a vacuum of –90 kPa (–0.9 kgf/cm2, –13.0 psi, –0.9 bar).
Do not remove brake booster pressure sensor.
Removal and reinstallation will spoil its original performance.
If faulty condition is observed, replace brake booster assembly with new one.

s1.ptxt: Connect SUZUKI scan tool to DLC (1).
Set ignition “ON”, and select “Brake Booster Pressure Sensor” in “Data list” mode on SUZUKI scan tool.
Check parameter displayed on SUZUKI scan tool at each negative pressure specified. Refer to Scan Tool Data .
If the parameter is not as shown in the table, check the following points.

item.ptxt: Brake booster pressure sensor (1) and grommet (2) for installation

s1.ptxt: Remove brake booster with brake master cylinder assembly (1).
Check brake booster pressure sensor output voltage as follows.
If check result is not as specified, replace brake booster.

attention4.ptxt: Specified input voltage of this brake booster pressure sensor is between 4.8 and 5.2 V. Therefore, arrangement of three 1.5 V dry batteries (4.5 V) is not enough, and four 1.5 V dry batteries (6 V) exceeds the limit which may affect the sensor.
Use four 1.2 V chargeable batteries for this check.

s2.ptxt: Arrange four 1.2 V chargeable batteries (3) in series and check that total voltage is 4.8 – 5.2 V.
Connect special tool, voltmeter (4) and batteries to brake booster and brake booster pressure sensor (2) as shown in figure and set the tool in “VACUUM” mode.

attention3.ptxt: Before using special tool (vacuum pump gauge), read its Operator’s Manual to know how to use it.

s2.ptxt: Check that voltage varies gradually when negative pressure is gradually applied with special tool.

spec.title: Vacuum sensor reference voltage
spec.ptxt: Negative pressure 0 kPa (0.0 kgf/cm2, 0.0 psi, 0.0 bar): 3.4 – 4.2 V
Negative pressure –70 kPa (–0.7 kgf/cm2, –10.1 psi, –0.7 bar): 0.6 – 1.4 V
